Medium. Replay protection depends on the keeper remembering ids: the CLI reads seen ids but never writes them. On OK, append the id to the seen file (kept outside site/, so it is not published), and test that a second run of the same request is refused.
Low. The site check is skipped when there is no CNAME; refuse instead when the site cannot be determined.
answer_to_a_factory: Yes, enforce an endorsement, but only for keys after the first. The first key in requesters.json is Dinis's own, added by the keeper on Dinis's word in its own session. Every other key (the riskmandate team) must carry an endorsement signed by a listed owner key (Dinis's), over {fingerprint, person, site, expires}, and verify() refuses a key without a valid one. Since anyone with push can edit requesters.json, the endorsement is what stops a pushed-in key from instructing the keeper. Add it before any key other than Dinis's is listed.
